what: Live adversarial battle-test of the on-chain-at-reveal data-availability design on Base Sepolia (chainId 84532). Proves end-to-end that solution bytes ride the reveal-tx calldata, are bound on-chain by sha256==commitDaHash, are re-fetchable by an independent operator, that fraud is caught + rejected + net-positive for the operator, that the off-chain (large-certificate) path works and refuses tampered bytes, that the indexer rebuilds the frontier + archives calldata, and that a realistic 114 KB solution goes fully on-chain.

tests.claim: 58-byte solution rode the reveal-tx calldata; full lifecycle fund->commit->reveal->finalize->close->claim->reclaim (7 signed txs); sha256(calldata)==on-chain commitDaHash anchor; permanenceHash=ZeroHash (NO Arweave receipt needed).
Against live chain state (committed submission #2), the contract accepts the correct bytes and REVERTS tampered/empty reveals — the on-chain sha256 bind cannot be bypassed.

A malicious solver revealed valid-hashing lying-claim bytes on-chain (131 B) claiming improvement 1 vs true 0. An INDEPENDENT operator fetched the bytes FROM THE REVEAL CALLDATA (no DA store), re-ran the verifier, found it fraudulent, and challenged. The resolver upheld it: submission REJECTED, operator NET-POSITIVE (won the forfeited solver bond).

On an onchainDa=false instance, the solver posted bytes to an off-chain content-addressed store and revealed EMPTY calldata (0x). An operator located the blob in the store, verified sha256==anchor, re-ran the verifier, and challenged the fraudulent claim.

A VALID off-chain submission (#2) had its store blob corrupted (1 byte flipped). The operator detected sha256(fetched)!=on-chain anchor, logged a DA FAULT, and REFUSED to act (did not wrongly challenge a valid submission). The off-chain integrity gate holds.

verified.operator_action: DA FAULT — refused tampered bytes, left for retry (no challenge)

tests.claim: The indexer reconstructed the full settlement state from events (9/9 cross-checks vs chain) AND archived the on-chain reveal calldata: recovered the bytes from the reveal tx, verified sha256==anchor, pinned by CID. The pinned blob hashes to its CID key. Idempotent (re-run: 1 already-pinned). This is the honest replacement for Arweave permanence for the >18-day later-delta tail.

A realistic 113,745-byte (114 KB) hadamard-668 solution went FULLY on-chain in the reveal calldata; sha256==anchor verified; finalized. Reveal used 4,578,570 gas (well under a Base block; validates the 1 MiB on-chain ceiling). On Base Sepolia the reveal cost ~0.0000275 ETH; on mainnet the L1 data-availability cost is the real driver (as the cost analysis flagged).

summary: 7/7 live tests passed. The on-chain-at-reveal DA design is validated end-to-end on Base Sepolia: bytes ride the reveal tx and are consensus-bound to the commit anchor; the integrity gate cannot be bypassed; an independent operator polices fraud (on-chain via calldata AND off-chain via a store, refusing tampered bytes) and is net-positive; the indexer rebuilds the frontier and archives calldata for the long tail; and a 114 KB solution goes fully on-chain. No Arweave dependency anywhere in the path.
